tagline.text: A curtain-like waterfall in a jungle gorge beside Suyo town, with the remains of an old power plant

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (more water in the rainy season)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–2,000 (excluding round-trip transport from Manila; local transport and meals)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Laoag International Airport (LAO) or overland via the Baguio area

children.text: Dawara Falls, close to the town of Suyo in Ilocos Sur, is a curtain-style waterfall where water breaks and tumbles down a rugged rock face. You reach it by a hanging bridge and a forest trail, and you can also see traces of an old hydropower plant.
Dawara Falls is in Suyo, a mountain town at the southern end of Ilocos Sur, close to the foothills of Abra and the Cordillera. Suyo is about
98 km
from Vigan and about
328 km
from Manila, and the municipality has 8 barangays. The falls belong to Barangay Poblacion, the town center, and on the map they lie within about
1 km
of the Suyo municipal hall. That makes them one of the easiest waterfalls to reach in Suyo. Locally the name is also spelled Darawa.

What sets this waterfall apart is that the water does not fall in one drop but breaks into many strands and scatters over the rough rock face. Travel bloggers have therefore given it a nickname that means something like a curtain. The Suyo municipal tourism page describes it as larger and taller than the nearby Sangbay ni Ragsak Falls. Heights differ from source to source, from about
to around 20 m, so it is best to think of it simply as a big waterfall rather than rely on one number.

Another story survives beside the falls. This stream once fed the Dawara mini-hydro power plant built by the Ilocos Sur Electric Cooperative (ISECO). The plant was buried by a landslide triggered by Super Typhoon Nitang on August 1, 1983, and was never restored, so only traces remain beside the forest trail. The large pipe half hidden on the left side of the falls is a remnant of that old waterway.

For travelers, the appeal of Dawara Falls is that you can enjoy jungle, a hanging bridge, and the sound of a waterfall in half a day with little preparation. It is usually combined with the other Suyo waterfalls, such as Sangbay ni Ragsak and Kaman-itil, in a one- or two-day plan. It is not widely known, so many days it is quiet, but signage and facilities are limited too. Keep that in mind when you plan. Here is some advice for first-timers. Suyo is too far to do as a round trip from Manila in one day, so the practical options are to take an overnight bus and arrive in Tagudin at dawn, or to sleep a night in Vigan or Candon first. The falls themselves involve only a short walk, but getting to and from town takes most of the day. Information on site is limited and you can lose your way, so ask the municipal tourism office or local residents about the route and current conditions first. If the Ilocos coast is about sand and heritage sites, Suyo shows the inland side, with mountains, rivers, and waterfalls. It is a good place to spend a day between Vigan and Laoag.

blocks.title: A curtain waterfall breaking into many strands

children.text: The water spreads wide as it strikes the uneven rock face. On days with plenty of water, spray reaches you from a distance. Even in the dry season a misty spray drifts around, so protect your camera and phone from water.
Walking a cement-paved path of about
1.2 km

from town, you come to an old hanging bridge over the river. Crossing the river that flows down from the falls and looking down into the gorge is a short but memorable stretch. The bridge is old, so cross one or two people at a time.

After the bridge, a shaded forest trail follows the river. The walk is short, so families with children and trekking beginners can try it. Part of the fun is hearing the sound of water grow louder among the dense trees.

blocks.title: The hydropower plant ruins left by Typhoon Nitang

children.text: Beside the forest trail are the remains of the Dawara mini-hydro plant, buried by the 1983 landslide. It is not set up as a tourist attraction, so it is best seen as a piece of local history. The large pipe on the left of the falls is also known to be part of the same facility.

blocks.title: A resting spot around the plunge pool

children.text: The riverbed below the falls is described as shallow because of erosion. So it suits wading, photos, and sitting on rocks to rest rather than deep swimming. If you want to swim, check the water depth yourself near the point where you cross the river upstream.

blocks.title: A base for Suyo's waterfall circuit

children.text: Suyo has several well-known waterfalls, including Sangbay ni Ragsak and Kaman-itil Falls. Dawara is the closest to town, so it works well as the start or the finish of your route. Some local reviewers rank it among the top waterfalls in Ilocos Sur.

blocks.title: Everyday life in a small mountain town

children.text: Poblacion on the way to the falls is a quiet mountain town. Adding a market visit and a local meal lets you glimpse everyday inland Ilocos life rather than a tourist spot. Locals are generally friendly when you ask for directions.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: Round trip from town to the falls

children.text: Arrive at the Bitalag junction or in Suyo town, and ask the municipal tourism staff whether you need to register your visit.
Start walking from Poblacion along the cement-paved path. It is about
1.2 km
to the hanging bridge.
Cross the old hanging bridge and enter the forest trail along the river. The trail leads toward the power plant ruins.
Arrive at the viewpoint of the falls. The path down to the river is badly eroded, so go down slowly.
Take photos and rest, then return the same way. It takes about
30 minutes
on foot to get back to town.
Have lunch at a town restaurant, then head to the next waterfall or start your return trip.
The municipal tourism page says it takes
15–20 minutes
on foot from the Poblacion bridge to the falls, while a travel blog says it takes about
5 minutes
from the hanging bridge to the falls viewpoint. The difference seems to come from different starting points.

items.subtitle: Dawara and Sangbay ni Ragsak in one day

children.text: Take a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) from Suyo to Barangay Patoc-ao.
Register at the entrance of Sangbay ni Ragsak Falls and walk to the falls.
Return to Suyo town and have lunch.
Walk to Dawara Falls. Pass the hanging bridge and forest trail and see the falls.
Return to town and travel on to Tagudin.
In the shorter days of November to January, start earlier. After rain, check the river level and trail conditions locally first.
Take an Ilocos-bound bus (Partas, Viron, Dominion, Florida, and others) heading to Candon, Vigan, Laoag, or Bangued in Abra.

You can also get off before the Kimpusa Bridge and walk the cement-paved footpath to the hanging bridge.
It is about

from Vigan to Suyo. Take the Ilocos national highway south and turn toward Suyo at Tagudin.
From Baguio or Sagada the road is mountainous, so allow plenty of time. We could not confirm a direct service, so ask locally.
Suyo gets about 1,800 mm of rain a year, with the most rain from May to October. Daytime highs are about
. Walking in the dry season is safer than in the rainy season, when the forest trail gets slippery.

One visitor wrote that the falls look best in July and September. That probably means high water, but the eroded trail and river level can become dangerous then. Avoid visiting right after heavy rain.

Suyo does not have many large hotels. Many travelers stay in nearby Tagudin or Candon and visit as a day trip. If you want to stay in Suyo itself, asking the municipal tourism staff about available lodging is the surest way.

There are said to be no shops around the falls. Prepare water, snacks, and a packed lunch in town. Near the town and the Tagudin market you can easily try Ilocano noodles, grilled meat, and local vegetable dishes.

For a day trip, it is convenient to have breakfast in Tagudin or town and lunch at a town restaurant after you return from the falls. Restaurant hours are not regular, so it is safer to bring a packed lunch.
Before you go, ask the Suyo municipal hall or tourism staff how to register your visit and what the current fee is. Check the latest announcements to be safe.
The hanging bridge is old. Do not cross with several people at once; cross slowly in single file.
The path down to the river is unstable because of erosion. Non-slip shoes and gloves help.
The spray from the falls is heavy, so keep your camera and phone in a waterproof pouch. They get wet even in the dry season.
Take your trash back with you. The area beside the forest trail is also where local residents live.
If you are doing it on the same day as Sangbay ni Ragsak, start early. The trail gets dark in the afternoon.
Download an offline map in your map app beforehand to make navigation easier.
Prepare plenty of cash. Many small towns have places that do not accept cards.
Starting from Poblacion in town, the cement-paved path is easy to walk. Wear sandals with straps or sneakers rather than flip-flops.
The weather can change quickly, so bring a raincoat, and ask locals whether it has rained upstream before going down to the river.
After heavy rain the river level rises quickly and the path down to the river becomes very slippery, so postpone your visit.
The section down to the river is eroded and it is easy to lose your footing.
Below the falls the water is shallow and rocky, so jumping in can cause injury. Swim only after checking the water depth yourself.
The hanging bridge is old and dangerous if many people cross at once.
Landslides and rockfalls can occur in the rainy and typhoon seasons. It was also a landslide from Super Typhoon Nitang that buried the power plant.
Do not climb on or enter the ruined power plant structures.
Another Suyo waterfall that starts from Barangay Patoc-ao; the name means falls of happiness. It is under
20 minutes
on foot, and combining it with Dawara is a common route.
A waterfall in Suyo that is also known locally by another nickname. Many people include it in a Suyo waterfall itinerary. Check the trail conditions locally.
A waterfall in Santa Maria, which one reviewer called their favorite in Ilocos Sur for its width and spectacle. It needs a separate trip from Suyo.
A UNESCO World Heritage city about
98 km
north of Suyo. If you stay one more day after the waterfalls, it is a good place to add a heritage-city walk.
